claims.text: Damaged high-value nickel-based superalloy components exhibit coarse grains, residual casting or weld-induced defects, and localized stress concentrations that make them vulnerable to hot cracking.
Friction Stir Processing can be applied in a double-pass configuration to repair a damaged alloy surface.
Suitable FSP parameters for the proposed nickel-based superalloy are approximately 800–1200 rpm and 20–40 mm/min.
The FSP temperature should be maintained below approximately 0.6Tm.
Keeping FSP below the melting point avoids liquid-phase defects associated with fusion processing.
FSP induces severe plastic deformation that leads to dynamic recrystallization.
Dynamic recrystallization during optimized FSP forms a fine, equiaxed surface-grain layer.
Optimized FSP minimizes microsegregation in the processed surface layer.
Optimized FSP reduces residual stress in the processed surface layer.
FSP eliminates casting or welding defects and associated stress-concentration sites through dynamic recrystallization.
The refined surface microstructure improves hardness and crack resistance.
The FSP-modified microstructure provides improved barrier properties against wear and corrosion.
The FSP-treated nickel-based superalloy surface will have approximately 20–30% higher microhardness than fusion-weld-repaired and untreated surfaces.
The FSP-treated surface will have markedly greater hot-cracking resistance than fusion-weld-repaired and untreated surfaces.
The FSP-treated surface will have markedly greater wear resistance than fusion-weld-repaired and untreated surfaces.
The FSP-treated surface will have markedly greater corrosion resistance than fusion-weld-repaired and untreated surfaces.
Untreated and fusion-weld-repaired surfaces are more prone to hot cracking because of coarse grains, residual defects, and high local stress concentrations.
The benefits of FSP will be less pronounced when its parameters are not optimized.
The anticipated improvements are limited to service conditions within a moderate temperature range.
Exact improvements in hardness and crack resistance depend on parameter optimization and tool design.
